messages:
sophia: Hey team — noticed a throughput dip on prod around 17:20 UTC last night, batch utilization dropped and queue depth spiked. Can we add focused telemetry to understand if the continuous batcher heuristics or KV cache misses are the root cause?

liam: saw that too. p50 latency for short prompts jumped ~1.8x, tokens/sec down ~25% for model-raven-1. Profiling indicates more small batches being emitted (avg batch size down from 6.2 -> 3.9).

nate: re: KV cache — I instrumented cache hit rates per-request last week; rough numbers show per-shard hit_rate fell from 92% to 82% during the window. Could be causing more generation steps per request.

jen: can we get a dashboard with these slices: batch_size distribution (histogram), batch_utilization (% used slots), queue_depth (p50/p95), tokens/sec, and KV cache hit rate? Also per-model and per-queue labels.

kai: agree. Also add a heatmap of batch formation latency (time from enqueue -> batch dispatch) and a small table of most frequent queue policies firing (e.g., max_wait, min_tokens, token_budget).

sophia: proposed minimal PromQL for batch_util: 
```
# batch utilization % across all workers
sum(rate(batcher_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) / sum(rate(batcher_token_capacity_total[1m])) * 100
```
This gives overall utilization but we need breakdowns per model, per-worker pool.

liam: for queue depth: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(batcher_queue_depth_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))` — then show p50/p95. For token/sec drop alerts: something like `sum(rate(batcher_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model) < 0.75 * avg_over_time(sum(rate(batcher_tokens_emitted_total[1m])) by (model)[1h:])`

nate: we should correlate kernel selection flips too. We sometimes auto-switch kernels for long context; if kernel change happens mid-batch it can throttle throughput. Add label `kernel_variant` to batcher metrics and track `kernel_switch_count` per-minute.

jen: add a small panel that maps: kernel_variant + quantization_profile -> p50 latency and batch_util. That will help spot regressions when we onboard new quantized kernels.

kai: on alerts: I'd set two alerts to start: 1) High queue depth + low tokens/sec sustained 5m -> paging to oncall. 2) Drop in batch_util > 30% vs baseline 15m -> paging to eng-runtime. We can tune after initial run.

infra-bot: deploy reported: rollout v2-batcher-heuristic at 202.54.12.19 applied 1793455100 -> success. No immediate deploy errors recorded.

sophia: action items: (1) jen + liam add dashboard panels (2) nate add kernel_variant and kv_hit_rate labels to batcher exporter (3) kai draft alerts and thresholds — target: dashboard + alerting live by EOD tomorrow. I can help with model slices for raven-1 and sage-lite.

liam: quick note — KV cache instrumentation needs low-overhead counters. Nate, try a sampled counter: `kv_requests_total{hit=\"true\"}` and `kv_requests_total{hit=\"false\"}` aggregated per-shard. Preferably exported as rate over 1m.

nate: yep plan is to emit `kv_hit_rate = rate(kv_requests_total{hit=\"true\"}[1m]) / rate(kv_requests_total[1m])`. Will add labels `shard` and `model`.

jen: UI ask: add time-range selector defaults: last 1h, overlay baseline 24h avg, and toggle to view raw/normalized tokens/sec. Also a small drilldown to individual worker traces.

kai: for token budget targets: propose target per-batch token budget of 2048 for raven-1 during peak, with autoscaler rule to increase worker pool if avg queue_wait > 200ms and batch_util > 60%. Thoughts?

sophia: that seems reasonable. One caveat — some clients submit very long system prompts that blow up token budgets; we should surface a percentile of request token counts and add a guard for single-request token_count above 75th pct.

liam: agreed. Also include a regression panel that compares current vs baseline for kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, tokens_per_sec. Make it easy to see correlated deltas.

jen: I'll sketch the dashboard layout and paste a mock PromQL and panel IDs in #dash-mockups later. For now I'll create panels: 1) Batch size histogram, 2) Batch util timeseries, 3) Queue depth p50/p95, 4) Tokens/sec, 5) KV hit rate, 6) Kernel switches heatmap, 7) Top offending requests table.

nate: will push exporter changes in a PR and add unit tests. ETA: 6h.

kai: I'll create initial alert rules in alertmanager with quiet windows for the first 24h to avoid noisy pages while we iterate.

sophia: perfect. If anyone spots a regression in the meantime, ping me directly. Thanks — this dashboard should help us root-cause whether it's batching heuristics, KV misses, or kernel selection/regression. :thumbsup:
